HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE AT ALLAHABAD ?Court No. - 84 Case :- CRIMINAL MISC. BAIL APPLICATION No. - 4240 of 2023 Applicant :- Kuldeep Opposite Party :- State of U.P.

entities.text: HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE AT ALLAHABAD
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Counsel for Applicant :- Rajendra Kumar Srivastava Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
Supplementary affidavit filed today on behalf of applicant is taken on record.
Heard Sri Rajendra Kumar Srivastava, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Ravi Kant Kushwaha, learned AGA for the State-respondent.

The instant application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No. 85 of 2020, under Sections 323, 307, 498A, 506 I.P.C. and Section 3/4 Dowry Prohibition Act, Police Station- Shikohabad, District- Firozabad during pendency of the trial in the court below.

Applicant is elder brother-in-law (jeth) of the victim and as per allegation, he along with his other family members used to torture the victim for want of dowry and ablazed her by pouring kerosene oil due to which she sustained burn injuries.

Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that the entire allegations made against the applicant are totally false and baseless and applicant has been made accused in the present matter only due to reason that he was elder brother of the husband of victim.
He further submitted that he neither ever demanded any dowry nor tortured victim in any manner.

He further submitted that applicant did Kuldeep vs State Of U.P. on 21 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45425681/
1 not participate in the alleged incident and it appears that while making food victim sustained minor burn injuries and thereafter, her uncle falsely implicated husband of the victim and his entire family members including applicant.

He next submitted from perusal of the injury report of victim, it appears that all the injuries were simple in nature except one swelling which was found on her chest admittedly there is no allegation against applicant that he caused this injury and as per the statement of the victim recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C., the husband of the victim thrown boiled oil upon her due to which she sustained burn injury on her leg.

It was further alleged that thereafter applicant and her mother-in-law caught hold her and ablazed her but medical report of the victim completely belies the allegation as except superficial burn on her leg, no burn injury was found on the body of the victim.
He further submitted that applicant is not having any criminal history and in the present matter he is in jail since 13.09.2022.

Per contra, learned AGA opposed the prayer for bail and submitted that applicant is elder brother of the husband of the victim and he used to torture her and also made assault and tried to ablaze her but could not dispute the fact that victim only sustained one superficial burn injury on her leg and this injury was attributed by the victim in her statement recorded under Section 161 Cr.P.C. to her husband.
I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of case.

Applicant and others were made accused in the present matter on the basis of general and omnibus allegations made in the first information report but when the statement of victim was recorded then along with general allegations, she specifically stated that applicant and her mother-in-law caught hold her and they set fire to her and in the statement she also stated that her husband thrown upon her boiled oil due to which she sustained burn injury on her leg.

From perusal of medical report of the victim, it appears that she sustained only one superficial burn injury on her leg, which is specifically attributed by her to her husband, therefore, medical report of the victim does not support her allegation that applicant and her mother-in-law also caused burn injury to her.
Applicant is 'jeth' of the victim and he is not having any criminal history and he is in jail since 13.09.2022.
Therefore, in view of the discussion made above, in my view applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
In the light of discussions made above, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

Let the applicant - Kuldeep be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.

(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
In case of breach of any of the above conditions, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicant.
